dedupe_keys.name: refit smart home study building surveys sensors and electrical load measurements for 20 uk homes

description: REFIT was a 2013 to 2015 study in which 20 UK homes were turned into smart homes with smart meters, programmable thermostats and radiator valves, and motion, door and window sensors, producing two linked open datasets. It was run by Loughborough, Strathclyde and East Anglia universities with ten industry partners under the EPSRC BuildTEDDI programme; the Smart Home dataset is maintained by Steven Firth at Loughborough (published 2017, updated 2019) and the cleaned electrical loads by David Murray at Strathclyde (2016). The Smart Home dataset has building surveys of the 20 homes, sensor measurements before and after installation, and nearby weather station data; the load dataset gives aggregate and appliance-level consumption in watts every 8 seconds, cleaned for duplicates, sensor limits and gaps. Coverage: 20 households in the UK, October 2013 to June 2015. Access: Loughborough and Strathclyde repositories, about 100 MB and 490 MB. Licence: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0; free. Caveats: a small sample of homes. Simulation uses: occupant behaviour, retrofit advice, load disaggregation and demand response models. Related records: OccDem and the GB National Energy Efficiency Data-Framework.
